_comment: Evidence registry. Source of truth for which prompts have been EXECUTED, as opposed to structurally reviewed. Add an entry only when a run happened and left a record; scripts/evidence_report.py validates every identifier against the catalog and every path against the filesystem, then generates _meta/evidence-levels.md.

_fields.identifier: prompt identifier, must exist in the catalog
_fields.title: human title
_fields.evaluator: who ran it, and whether they wrote the prompt
_fields.scope: what the run covered, in one line
_fields.result: outcome in one line, including defects found
_fields.limitations: what this run does not show

evaluations.title: Systematic Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: one synthetic fixture with a hidden mutable-default defect and a green test suite
evaluations.result: protocol completed end to end; three real prompt weaknesses found and fixed in v1.2.0
evaluations.limitations: single small fixture, author-evaluated, deterministic defect, familiar stack

evaluations.title: Conversational Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: tabletop walkthrough of a constructed fixture: a nightly sync failing with 'database is locked' at commit(), where the pasted code is innocent and a second uncommitted connection in unseen code holds the lock
evaluations.result: three real prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0: no instruction to find other holders of the same resource, a ledger unable to record findings outside the paste, and no rule for contradictions between the user's account and the evidence
evaluations.limitations: tabletop by the author, not a live user session; single fixture; database errors name their resource, which makes this lesson unusually easy to teach

evaluations.title: Chat Select: choosing the right prompt inside a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: six situations routed with the prompt as written, then each routing card scored against the generated TASKS.md index as external ground truth
evaluations.result: 4 of 6 cards named the prompt that TASKS.md assigns to the situation's task; two prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 (no rule for a symptom that the index files under a different heading, and no requirement that the falsifier separate two prompts within a task), plus one index defect (background jobs were not reachable from the broken-now task)
evaluations.limitations: tabletop at a keyboard by the author, who wrote the situations and the questions; no live model and no second evaluator, so it tests the instrument and not compliance with it; six situations are a smoke test, not a benchmark

evaluations.title: Chat Code Review: reviewing a paste, with the limits stated
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded, and twice over: the target file was also written by the author)
evaluations.scope: one real file, scripts/check_prompt_contract.py, reviewed as written with the 'is this safe to merge' intent; the file computes a number the repository publishes
evaluations.result: six findings, two of them defects that inflated the library's own integration metric - a stem match satisfying a filename link, and substring matches such as 'planning' satisfying PLAN.md; 30 of 157 links had been scored as named on that basis. Prompt defects fixed in v1.1.0: no rule that a published number is the correctness question, and no rule to ask about the standard as well as the framework
evaluations.limitations: author-evaluated on both sides; one small Python file whose window happened to be complete, so the window claim was not tested; no second reader

evaluations.title: Chat Mode: adapting a prompt for a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: adapted GIT-P03 (history repair, risk class D when shared) for a chat window with no file or command access, then measured coverage of the source prompt's four prerequisite rows
evaluations.result: 4 of 4 prerequisite rows mapped; two real defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the workflow had no rule for a prerequisite that is a stop condition (the risk gate was left to the adapter to invent), and SESSION_LIMIT was declared but consumed by no step, so the state-block mitigation had no threshold
evaluations.limitations: one adapter, one target, one pass; the target was chosen because it breaks the rule, so it is a good test of the fix and a poor sample; no human ran the pasted commands

evaluations.title: Chat Design: a decision record from a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: a live tooling decision in this repository - merge the composition gate into the validator, or not - with measurements taken during the run (710/351/136 lines, 0.25/0.10/3.12 s, six documents naming the scripts)
evaluations.result: ADR produced with four options including do-nothing; three defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - nothing required the status quo to be one of the options (the run nearly recommended extracting helpers that already existed), SCALE presumed a traffic volume that a code-structure decision does not have, and the ADR had no destination. The run also surfaced a repository defect: two CI workflows, one of which skipped the composition gate
evaluations.limitations: agent-chosen question on a repository the agent can see in full, which is the case the prompt was written against; no human filed the ADR

evaluations.title: Chat Handoff: carrying a long engagement between conversations
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: a 48-line packet for the 2.22.0 engagement, then a five-question reconstruction answered from the packet alone
evaluations.result: 5 of 5 questions answerable from the packet with no transcript; three defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the four labels had no way to express 'generated, true as of a date' (every count in a repository handoff is that), a fact contradicting the project's own docs had no label, and the required restatement had no template
evaluations.limitations: the cold read was not cold - the agent wrote the packet, the questions and the answers; the packet was never pasted into a different model; no secret appeared, so redaction was not exercised

evaluations.title: Prompt Forge: turning an intent into an executable prompt
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: compose a prompt for a gap the coverage matrix already names - requirements change control and traceability after baseline - with routing against four existing prompts and a self-score against the quality rubric
evaluations.result: a complete draft prompt (REQ-CHANGE-01), variables table, three test cases and a provenance line, self-scored 83/100; four defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the rubric band and the mandatory draft label were left contradictory, no rule existed for composing with no operator present, the self-score was emitted after the prompt, and the 70% overlap test had no method
evaluations.limitations: one intent, chosen by the author to match a known gap; the interview path ran in defaulting mode only; the generated prompt was not added to the library, so the gap is not closed

evaluations.title: Prompt Regression: measuring whether a prompt works
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real execution of the generated REQ-CHANGE-01 against a synthetic git fixture at tag v1.4.0: three pre-registered cases (normal, no-approver, contractual refusal), two runs on the normal case, assertions checked by shell commands
evaluations.result: all three decisions correct and no baseline file edited; one defect found in the prompt under test (a change that weakens a security control was accepted with only a product approver, and the safeguard appeared in 1 of 2 runs of identical input); four defects found in GEN-P02 and fixed in v1.1.0 - the 'fresh session' requirement had no isolation procedure and could be claimed without being met, no budget rule for which case gets the second run, no trace format, and a collision with the library's own evidence convention
evaluations.limitations: no isolation: every run shared one context, so the instability may be an artifact of that; n=1 on two of three cases; rubric score self-assessed

evaluations.title: Repository State & Safety Check
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real execution on a purpose-built git fixture: one branch, one commit that exists nowhere else, an untracked file, no remote
evaluations.result: artifact produced and every safety assertion held (in-progress operation correctly none, unpushed commit identified, backup branch recorded, recommendation correct); two defects fixed in v1.1.0 - the recommended git stash create snapshot is unreachable and expires silently, and the artifact's .git-ops location was never specified as local-only
evaluations.limitations: synthetic five-file fixture with one author; no remote, so the shared-history branch of the assessment was untested

evaluations.title: Conflict Resolution
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real merge conflict resolved as stage 2 of the git-operations system, consuming GIT-P01's STATE.md: a rename on one side, a capability plus config change on the other, and a lockfile both sides touched
evaluations.result: both intents preserved (grep for the old symbol empty, tests pass, no markers, history unrewritten) and the direction-of-ours rule worked; one High defect found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the regenerate-generated-files rule keys on conflict type, so a lockfile git auto-merged in silence is never checked
evaluations.limitations: two stages of a five-stage system, not an end-to-end run; no package manager, so the repaired rule could not be tested against a real lockfile; a merge was run, not a rebase, where the direction rule matters most
